messages.content: Can you help me find public libraries in New York, NY that have a Reading Room and Fiction section, and then in Los Angeles, CA that offer Wi-Fi and have a Children Section, and finally in Chicago, IL that have a Cafe and a Reading Room?

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with facilities. The user wants libraries in New York, NY with Reading Room and Fiction section. Then in Los Angeles, CA with Wi-Fi and Children Section. Finally in Chicago, IL with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function three times. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings or array? It says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems ambiguous: maybe facilities can be an array of strings? The type shows union of string or array? Actually it says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So maybe it's either a single string or an array of strings. We'll pass array of strings.

Thus we call:

public_library_find_nearby({"location":"New York, NY","facilities":["Reading Room","Fiction"]})

Then similar for LA and Chicago.

We need to output the results. We'll call function thrice.
